entries.test: Public technical evaluations of Mythos would establish whether Anthropic demonstrated recursive self-improvement or substantive capabilities beyond improved LLM benchmark performance.
entries.note: The technical assertions are checkable; the claimed marketing motive is not independently established by them.
He explicitly endorses a possibility, qualified by alternative outcomes.

entries.test: Public billing changes, subsidy estimates, and subsequent customer cancellations and financial results would test whether withdrawing subsidies caused the deterioration described.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies an economic reading of 'fall apart.' Intentional concealment remains a separate motive allegation.

entries.test: Public customer spending disclosures, revenue breakdowns, and Anthropic's organizational usage-reporting features would test whether experimental spending with inadequate visibility accounted for the vast majority of its recent revenue increase.
entries.note: Limited disclosure makes this difficult to verify, not inherently uncheckable.
The projected revenue collapse and cost increase are explicitly qualified by 'likely.' The billing and pricing assertions are separately factual.
'Every chance' states a possibility rather than a firm outcome.
'Hard to see how' expresses doubt about winning customers over rather than a firm prediction. The parenthetical claim about fatal cuts is firmer.
The cost increase underlying the explanation is hedged with 'appear.' The fundraising amount is independently checkable, subject to the closing condition.
The substantive inference concerns companies' private confidence in their products. Subsidy levels alone cannot establish that belief.

entries.test: Public provider cost data, customer prices, and measured financial returns would test whether generative AI is becoming cheaper and whether its economic value covers its costs.
entries.note: The surrounding economics discussion gives 'business model' a plain reading concerning commercial viability.

entries.test: Technical proofs and operational studies, together with token billing and margin data, would test whether unavoidable hallucinations and continuing training requirements increase customer costs under unprofitable pricing.
entries.note: The assertion of mathematically guaranteed hallucinations is a substantive technical claim despite the surrounding invective.
The claim attributes spending to customers' private convictions and disconnection from work. 'I believe' alone is not the reason for excluding it.

entries.test: Public company cost-cutting announcements and accounts linking subsequent admissions about AI returns to Uber's COO's remarks would test the proposed connection.
entries.note: Giving others 'permission' is presented as a causal explanation for their public admissions.

entries.test: Public evidence available at publication of profitable open-source model hosting or competitive deployments at comparable scale would test the asserted absence of proof.
entries.note: This claims an absence of demonstrated results, not that such results are impossible.
Continued purchasing does not establish the private motivations attributed to the vast majority of customers.

entries.test: Customer retention and payment data following charges for actual token consumption would test whether the vast majority refuse to pay for that consumption.
entries.note: In context, this is a firm prediction about willingness to pay when subsidies are removed.

entries.test: Applicable accounting standards and public descriptions of OpenAI's and Anthropic's training expenditures would establish whether those costs qualify as cost of goods sold or capital expenditure.
entries.note: 'Their' refers to OpenAI and Anthropic; the normalization broadens this to AI labs generally.

entries.test: Anthropic's financial results immediately following a price cut or customer churn would test whether either event puts it deeply into losses.
entries.note: The conditional financial prediction is checkable. The alleged purpose of the compute discount is a separate private-motive claim.
As bundled, this is an evaluative verdict about recklessness and Silicon Valley, without a specified failure outcome.

entries.test: Public cost, profitability, and customer payment data following data-center expansion and additional funding would test whether those changes produce the economic improvements he rules out.
entries.note: The profitability prediction is firm and undated; the current cost-trend assertion is already assessable.
The normalization silently changes 'dependence' to 'independence,' plausibly correcting a typo but reversing the literal wording. Absorption is explicitly qualified by 'likely.'
'May be the last' is explicitly tentative. The 'end of the dream' also lacks a shared empirical threshold.
'Neither' refers to Microsoft and Google; 'these companies' broadens the conclusion to include Amazon. Whether they care is a private attitude, not established by their public response.
